parameters.content:
## Notion HelpDesk: Inbound (Free tier)
by [Marcan et Co.](https://marcan.co)

## Who it's for
Small teams that answer customers from one support email address, already work in Notion, and want every request tracked as a Ticket without paying for a help desk.

## What it does
- Reads your Support address over IMAP and turns each new email into a Ticket in a Notion database (Status **New**), with the sender as its Requester in a Contacts database.
- Cleans the email first: the title is the subject without Re:/Fwd:/TR:/RV:, and the body drops quoted history and confidentiality notices and fixes broken accents. The text goes at the top of the Ticket, above your Tickets database's default template.
- Keeps attachments in the Ticket's **Attachments** property.
- Adds a reply in the same email thread to its Ticket as a comment instead of opening a new Ticket, with the reply's attachments on the comment.
- Skips an email that is already on a Ticket, so you can safely retry a failed execution from **Executions**.

## How to set up
About 15 minutes; the [setup guide](https://marcan.co/notion-helpdesk/) has every step, in English and French.
1. Duplicate the [Notion template](https://marcanetco.notion.site/Notion-HelpDesk-3ea524fadb0d80619080e48a163b2cf1) and connect a Notion integration to it, with the **Insert comments** capability.
2. Create an IMAP credential for your Support address (for Gmail, an app password) and select it in **Email received**.
3. Create a Notion credential with the integration's secret and select it in every HTTP Request node.
4. Paste the Tickets and Contacts database ids in **Settings**.
5. Send a test email to your Support address, check the Ticket, then publish the workflow.

## Want more?
The [Paid tier](https://marcan.co/notion-helpdesk/setup-service/) adds replies sent from Notion comments, Status changes with a Closing email, CC and forwarded-email handling, and error alerts. [Join the waitlist](https://marcan.co/notion-helpdesk/setup-service/#waitlist) to hear when it's out.
Rather have it done for you? With the [Setup service](https://marcan.co/notion-helpdesk/setup-service/#setup-service), Marcan et Co. sets up the Paid tier in your own n8n and Notion.

Free tier released under the MIT license. © 2026 Marcan et Co.

## 1. Receive
New emails in the Support address's inbox, one at a time. Your database ids are in **Settings**.

## 2. Skip duplicates, spot follow-ups
Cleans the email, skips it if its Message-ID is already on a Ticket, then checks its thread headers (In-Reply-To, References).

## 3. Follow-up: add a comment
A reply to an email already on a Ticket becomes a comment on that Ticket, starting with the author's name. Its attachments are uploaded in step 4 and go on the comment, 3 per comment. Its Message-ID is added to the Ticket last.

## 4. Store attachments
Uploads each attachment to Notion, for a new Ticket or a follow-up. A file Notion refuses (too large, unsupported type) is named with a ⚠️ on the Ticket or the comment instead.

## 5. Find or create the Requester
Looks up the sender in Contacts by email address, and creates the Contact if it's new.

## 6. Create the Ticket
Creates the Ticket from the Tickets database's default template, adds the email at the top, then stores its Message-ID. Without a default template, the email is the whole body. Any other Notion error stops the execution.

nodes.name: One email at a time
nodes.notes: Each email creates its Ticket before the next one is read, so two emails from a new person share one Contact.

nodes.name: Find Ticket
nodes.notes: Same Message-ID already a Ticket: the email was fetched twice, skip it.

nodes.name: Find thread Ticket
nodes.notes: The Ticket holding a Message-ID this email answers (In-Reply-To/References).

nodes.name: Add comment
nodes.notes: No retry: a comment that timed out may exist already, and a retry would post it twice.

nodes.name: Add Message-ID to Ticket
nodes.notes: Last, so a follow-up whose comment failed is added again on retry, not skipped.

nodes.name: Create Ticket
nodes.notes: From the Tickets database's default template. No retry: a create that timed out may still exist.

nodes.name: Store Message-ID
nodes.notes: Last, so an email whose add failed is created again on retry, not skipped.

nodes.name: Create Ticket without template
nodes.notes: The Tickets database has no default template: the email is the whole body.
